how: Drawn by eye by a Claude agent on 2026-11-25 on the LoRA-at-weight-1 pictures of Z10 (8 pairs x seeds 6001-6004), reading each 1024 x 1024 picture against a 64-pixel grid. Each box [x0, y0, x1, y1] in picture pixels covers one whole visible animal body (head, tail, legs, wings, tentacles), shadows and reflections excluded. Assignment rules, fixed before drawing: 1) if one body looks more like A and the other more like B in shape, assign by that; 2) if both look like the same animal or neither is clear, A is the left body and B the right (by box centre); 3) one body only: it goes to the animal it looks more like, the other box is null, layout 'one'; 4) three or more bodies (tiny ones included): box the two largest, assign them by rules 1 and 2, layout 'extra', the others named in the note. For 'extra' entries 'rule' is 4 and the note says whether rule 1 or 2 assigned the pair.
